result.output:
# Agent delivery through Entire branches

Coding agents publish locally validated work on task branches through Entire. The repository owner handles remote CI and merging to `main`.

## Solo-owner review policy

All coding agents publish routine changes without GitHub review requests or required human or automated code review. Review is optional when the owner asks for it. Keep local validation and existing CI workflows in place.

## Start from current main

1. Read this policy before code, Git, CI, or push actions. Confirm that `origin` points to the repository's `entire://` remote. Fetch `origin` and inspect the worktree. Preserve concurrent and unrelated changes.
2. Create a fresh `codex/<task>`, `claude/<task>`, or `antigravity/<task>` branch from current `origin/main` for each coherent batch.
3. Stage only files that belong to the batch. Run the relevant local validation and commit the changes. Check the latest `origin/main` before publication. If the base changed in ways that affect the batch, integrate those changes safely and rerun the affected local checks.

## Publish the branch

1. Push through `origin` with an explicit refspec, such as `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/codex/<task>`. If the user asks for an Entire Trail, use `entire agent-help trail` for the publication and linking commands.
2. Report the branch, commit SHA, local verification, and any acceptance work that remains. Continue with the next batch as requested. Remote CI status, GitHub review requests, pull requests, and merging are outside this delivery workflow.
3. If authentication expires, surface the official Entire login flow. Preserve branch protections and existing history. Never force-push or change the remote to deliver a task.

- **Meeting Rooms was already on main.** The uncommitted changes are an early draft of #1056, and #1057 refined it after that. The remaining differences are main's own later work, such as its switch to `@/` imports and the `flushSyncMessage` removal in #1039. Nothing from the draft needed porting.

**What I shipped**
- **Branch:** `claude/pp-audit-mode-canonical`, commit `f9f08082f`, pushed through Entire and based on the latest `origin/main`.

- **What I left out of the old copy:**
  - Its pp.md would have undone #939's Entire delivery step, so I kept main's version of that step.
  - Its AGENTS.md would have brought back the old "work directly on main" policy, so I left that out.
- **Checks:** `validate:capabilities`, `validate:mainline-workflows` and `git diff --check` pass. Remote CI wasn't checked, since branch-safety leaves CI and merging to you.

Every slash workflow in `.agent/workflows/*.md` (40 files, all except `branch-safety.md`) must contain one exact sentence. The sentence is enforced by `scripts/validate-mainline-workflows.js` (the `required` constant near line 8):

The owner handles remote CI and merging, and an Entire Trail is used only when the user asks for one. There is no "automatic Trail route" any more.

1. Read `branch-safety.md` and the validator.
2. Pick the replacement sentence. Suggested: "It defines delivery through Entire task branches; use an Entire Trail only when the user asks for one."

## 2026-11-19 — vi.spyOn(window.localStorage, ...) is a silent no-op under jsdom

**SEVERITY:** Medium (CI red on main; a failure-path test cannot simulate storage failure)
- BUG: `vi.spyOn(window.localStorage, 'getItem').mockImplementation(() => { throw ... })` never takes effect. jsdom's `Storage` is a legacy platform object with named properties, so defining `getItem` on the instance stores an item named "getItem" (`localStorage.length` becomes 1) while method lookups still hit `Storage.prototype.getItem`. - FIX: Spy on the prototype: `vi.spyOn(Storage.prototype, 'getItem')`, and assert `expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalled()` so a no-op spy fails loudly.

- FIX: `OnboardingPage` waits ("Loading your profile…" + Retry) until the profile has a uid; `loadUserProfile` keeps local edits whose `updatedAt` is newer than the stored copy (`profileUpdatedAtMs` shared with the listener).
- DIAGNOSIS THAT WORKED: subscribe to the store in the page and record every `userProfile` change with `new Error().stack`; it named `resetStoreForAccountBoundary` and `loadUserProfile` in one run after many selector guesses failed.
- PREVENTION: Any UI that edits account state must render only once that account's own data has loaded. Every loader that writes state after an `await` must not overwrite newer local edits. In e2e, seed store state only after the app's boundary reset and profile load have settled.

## 2026-11-23 — engine-dsp deploy fails with "Quota exceeded for total allowable CPU per project per region" (CLOUD_RUN_REGIONAL_CPU_QUOTA)

**SEVERITY:** Medium (main deploy run red; Hosting, rules and Functions had already deployed, so only the engine-dsp worker stayed on its old revision)
- BUG: In deploy run 45173897673 the "Deploy authenticated print preparation worker" step builds and rolls out `print-prep` and `engine-dsp` at the same time. Revision `engine-dsp-00720-qxf` was refused with `Quota exceeded for total allowable CPU per project per region` (seen with `gcloud run revisions list --service engine-dsp`); the step only printed "Creating Revision…failed" and a container-failed-to-start link, and the revision log had no container output because it never started.
- FIX: Rerun the failed job (`gh run rerun <id> --failed`) once the other rollout has finished; earlier revisions keep serving.
- DIAGNOSIS THAT WORKED: `gcloud run revisions list --service <svc> --limit 4 --format='value(name,status.conditions[0].status,status.conditions[0].message)'` gives the real reason when the deploy log only says the container failed to start.
- PREVENTION: Before calling a Cloud Run deploy failure a code problem, read the revision's condition message. If quota keeps recurring, deploy `print-prep` and `engine-dsp` one after the other in the workflow, or request more regional CPU quota.

**Not wired yet:** nine files would have become controls that do nothing or mislead you:
- **Theme toggle:** no light theme exists, so it would change nothing.
- **"Do not sell my data" toggle:** nothing reads the setting, so it would promise an opt-out that doesn't happen.
- **Territory rights panel:** release delivery ignores territory splits.
- **Session timeout screen:** any click dismisses it, so it isn't a real lock.
- **Five other files:** an older copy of something that already ships in the app.

The reason for each is recorded in the ledger as ISSUE-1727.

**What's left:** the remaining ~90 files are sorted by readiness in `docs/plans/wire-in-map-2026-11-28.md` on the branch. Jev's sorting is only a hint: it was unsure about most files and wrong on the ones I checked, so I check each file myself before wiring it.

content.text:
I deleted the bad branch and wired three more features into the app. That's 12 of the 129 unconnected files so far. It isn't perfect yet: about 75 files haven't been checked, and nothing has been tried in the logged-in app.

**Deleted:** `claude/prune-unreachable-renderer` is gone from the remote. It was deleting 20 helper files you want to keep, and none of them were ever deleted from `main`. A local backup is saved at `refs/backup/prune-unreachable-renderer` in case you ever want it back. Those 20 helpers are now listed in the wire map too; four of them are developer-only scripts or stubs and shouldn't be wired.

**Newly wired** (pushed to `claude/wire-unconnected-w1`):
- **Bug reports:** the app now remembers the last crash or error and which screen it happened on. "Report a bug" (Ctrl+Shift+B) fills that in for you if it happened in the last 10 minutes.
- **Marketing:** the campaign post editor has an "Improve with AI" button. It rewrites your current draft and puts the result back in the editor; nothing saves until you click Save.
- **Social:** clicking a post's author opens their profile, with a follow button and their posts, plus "Back to feed".

The typecheck, lint, the 717 tests in the affected areas, and the production build all pass. Remote CI hasn't run.

**Checked and not wired yet**, because each would have been a broken or misleading control:
- **Need backend work first:**
  - Community announcements to Discord/Slack/Telegram: the web app's security policy blocks those sites.
  - The import hub for existing files: the backend analyzes the uploads, but no one can read or see the results.
  - Territory rights: the delivery files sent to stores ignore territory splits.
  - The "do not sell my data" toggle: nothing honours it yet.
  - The theme toggle: there is no light theme.
- **Already exist in another form:** Veo video settings, the chat message list, the release status list, and the publishing earnings panels.
- **Waiting on your product call:** the organization switcher. Switching organizations is currently limited to dev builds on purpose.

Every reason is in the ledger (ISSUE-1727) and `docs/plans/wire-in-map-2026-11-28.md`.

Should I keep checking and wiring the ~75 remaining files, or would you rather decide the blocked ones first (the backend work, the organization switcher, a light theme)?
